Latvian Gas and Water Utilities Hit by Ransomware Attack, Services Disrupted

A large-scale ransomware attack on Latvia’s gas and water utilities sector has caused significant service disruptions across the country, industry officials confirmed on Thursday. The cyber attack, which began late Wednesday evening, targeted the central IT systems of several major providers—including Riga-based LatGasNet and Daugava Waterworks—crippling billing platforms and interrupting real-time monitoring of critical infrastructure.

As of Thursday afternoon, many customers in Riga and Liepāja reported difficulties accessing online payment services and delays in customer support response times. In some areas, automated water quality sensors and gas flow monitors have been rendered inoperative, forcing companies to switch to manual oversight. According to the Latvian Utilities Association, the incident has not yet led to widespread supply outages, but the risk of localized interruptions remains elevated.

“We are working around the clock to contain the breach and restore our systems,” said Andris Kļaviņš, spokesperson for LatGasNet. “Our primary focus is on maintaining safe and reliable supply for all customers, and we are coordinating closely with the national cybersecurity center and law enforcement.”

The attackers are believed to have encrypted critical databases and demanded payment in cryptocurrency, though no details of negotiations have been disclosed. Industry analysts estimate that as many as 120,000 residential and business accounts could be affected by the incident. The Utilities Workers’ Union has called for urgent government support to ensure staff safety and maintain essential operations.

“Utility companies have been investing in digital infrastructure, but this attack shows vulnerabilities remain,” said Inese Ozoliņa, chief analyst at Baltic Risk Advisors. “With IT systems offline, manual management increases the risk of errors and complicates regulatory compliance.”

The Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development stated that emergency protocols have been activated and a task force is overseeing the situation. “We urge the public to remain patient and report any service anomalies,” the ministry said in a statement.

At press time, restoration efforts were ongoing, with no estimated timeline for full recovery. The Latvian Utilities Association warned that customers should be vigilant for potential phishing emails or scams exploiting the disruption.
